content.title: 16 FOOD FACTS THAT SOUND MADE UP BUT {{AREN'T}}
facts: **Nutmeg** – just 2 whole grated nutmegs can cause hallucinations and dangerous poisoning. It's technically a mild hallucinogen in large doses.
**Carrots** – eating extreme amounts can literally turn your skin orange. It's a real condition called carotenemia, and it's harmless, just cosmetic.
**Cashews** – the ones you buy are never sold in-shell, because the shell contains a toxic oil related to poison ivy that must be carefully removed first.
**Apple seeds** – they contain a compound that turns into cyanide in your gut, but you'd need to chew and swallow hundreds of seeds for it to matter.
**Strawberries** – they're not technically a berry, but bananas and avocados botanically are. Fruit classification rarely matches the grocery aisle.
**Black pepper** – it was once so valuable in medieval Europe that it was used as currency to pay rent, taxes, and even dowries.
**Rhubarb** – the stalks are a popular dessert ingredient, but the leaves contain enough oxalic acid to be genuinely toxic if eaten in quantity.
**Chewing gum** – if swallowed, it does not stay in your stomach for 7 years. It passes through your digestive system mostly intact within days.
**Pineapple** – it contains an enzyme called bromelain that actively breaks down proteins, which is why your tongue can feel raw after eating a lot of it.
**Cold water** – drinking it does not burn extra calories in any meaningful way, despite the popular claim that your body works hard to warm it up.
**Lychee** – unripe lychee fruit has caused real, documented outbreaks of sudden illness in children in parts of India due to a toxin that drops blood sugar.
**Nutritional yeast** – it's a deactivated fungus, not a vegetable, yet it's one of the few plant foods that naturally contains vitamin B12 when fortified.
**Almonds** – wild bitter almonds contain enough natural cyanide compounds that eating a handful raw could theoretically be dangerous; cultivated sweet almonds are bred to be safe.
**Follow along** – for more surprising, verified food facts like this, every week.
content.caption:
The nutmeg fact genuinely surprises most people: your body converts a compound called myristicin into something chemically similar to amphetamines when you eat large amounts, which is why historic cases of 'nutmeg poisoning' involved real hallucinations and racing hearts. Pineapple is another one worth understanding — bromelain isn't just folklore, it's an actual protein-digesting enzyme strong enough that it's used commercially to tenderize meat, which is literally why your mouth tingles after a big bowl of it. And rhubarb's danger isn't a myth either: the leaves concentrate oxalic acid at levels high enough to affect your kidneys and nervous system, which is exactly why only the stalks ever made it into pie. Everyone's tolerance and body chemistry differs, so when in doubt, moderation is the safer bet.
